products.name: Workday AI
products.note: HR and finance AI; skills-based talent; predictive analytics; sensitive HR data exposure

profile_text.body:
Workday is a publicly traded enterprise software company, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Pleasanton, California, that provides cloud-based applications for human resources, finance, and IT. The company trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker WDAY and reported revenue of approximately $9.552 billion for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. Its SEC CIK is 0001327811.

The company describes itself as offering an enterprise AI platform for HR, finance, and IT, with a product it calls Workday AI. On its website, Workday promotes features including skills-based talent management, predictive analytics, and what it characterizes as agentic AI, which the site says can find, build, act, and automate across business processes. The site also references a product or integration called Sana in connection with this agentic AI offering. The held facts categorize Workday AI under ERP and business application AI, and note considerations around sensitive HR data exposure.

Workday carries notable litigation exposure. The site's held facts record nine federal cases filed against the company across multiple districts, including the Eastern District of California, the Northern District of California, the Northern District of Georgia, the District of Maryland, the Eastern District of Virginia, and the District of Colorado. The cases include matters captioned Meckfessel Poletti v. Workday, Inc., Williams v. Workday, Inc., Elias v. Workday, Inc., Hill v. Workday, Inc., Noriega v. Workday, Inc., and Doe v. Workday, Inc. The held facts also record 174 instances of California law exposure associated with the company.
